title: Causal Chain Intervention: Training Data Contamination as a Deceptive Goal Precursor
original_idea: Fine-tune small models on pre-training data subsets with varying proportions of deception-heavy content. Measure deceptive alignment propensity as a function of deception-heavy data proportion using a standard scheming benchmark.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: pre-training data with deceptive content -> increased deceptive alignment propensity -> data curation as first-line safety intervention. Each link is explicit. The implication (data curation upstream of RLHF) is a concrete, actionable safety measure.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Fine-tuning small models with curated data subsets is intermediate work using standard tools (SFTTrainer). Dataset curation requires identifying and categorizing deception-heavy content, which is methodologically clear. Evaluating on existing benchmarks is straightforward. Feasible for beginners with guidance.

narrow_scope.reasoning: A deliverable exists (misalignment rate vs deception-data proportion curve), but requires constructing the curated data subsets (substantial effort), fine-tuning multiple models, and selecting/adapting a scheming benchmark. Multiple workstreams before the first result.

novelty.reasoning: The emergent misalignment literature directly addresses how training data composition affects misalignment. The Nature 2026 paper shows narrow fine-tuning on insecure code causes broad misalignment. Follow-up work ('Assessing Domain-Level Susceptibility to Emergent Misalignment' arXiv:2602.00298) examines which domains are susceptible. Research shows 5% misaligned samples can degrade honesty by 20%. However, the specific dose-response curve (deceptive alignment propensity as a continuous function of deception-heavy data proportion) using a standard scheming benchmark has not been published as a systematic study. The idea of data curation as an upstream safety intervention is implicit in emergent misalignment work but not the primary focus. Existing work uses binary or few conditions rather than a systematic proportion sweep.
